title: Singleton (creational)
points: Exactly one instance of a class with a global access point.
Typical uses: config manager, connection pool, expensive clients such as AWS SDK clients (create once outside the Lambda handler).
trade: Same caveats as static: global state, hard to unit test, hides dependencies, breaks DIP. One per JVM, not cluster-wide. Mutable state must be thread-safe. Prefer a container-managed singleton (Spring bean) over a hand-written getInstance().
test: Why is a hand-written getInstance() Singleton hard to unit test, and what is the usual fix in Spring? Is it one instance across all your servers?
answer: Callers depend on the concrete class so you can't swap in a mock. In Spring let the container manage a singleton bean and inject it. No: it is one per JVM or container.

questions.question: Why is a hand-written getInstance() Singleton a problem for unit tests, and what does Spring offer instead?
options: It is slow; use a thread pool
Callers depend on the concrete class so it can't be mocked; use a container-managed singleton bean and inject it
It is not thread-safe; use synchronized everywhere
It can only hold constants; use static final
questions.explanation: Hidden global access breaks DIP. A Spring bean is still one instance but is injected, so tests can substitute a mock.
